DIGEST: Plan frozen at 4 gates after a cold critic materially changed it. The critic's decisive finding is one I would not have caught by re-reading my own plan: DC5's numerator, as I first wrote it, could not lose. A malformed call rejected by client-side schema validation never reaches the server, so counting from the server's own log would have credited the typed door with avoiding exactly the fumbles the instrument was blind to -- a win regardless of whether the door helps. The counting unit is now an invocation attempt read from the driving agent's record, identical across arms, with the server log demoted to corroboration. Two further changes follow the same shape: the measurement now gets an independent re-derivation it previously self-graded, and DC3's live positive control is disambiguated from DC3's test, which exercise different mechanisms (engine lease identity vs door instance reachability) and would otherwise have deadlocked the gate against a defect outside F's scope.
